A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpikeSR research and contain nine readable pages with matching scientific text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: Sections IV–V report original super-resolution experiments on AID, DOTA, and DIOR, along with component ablations and feature analyses in Tables I–V and Figures 5–9.

after.justification: The same original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative analyses are retained in Sections IV–V, Tables I–V, and Figures 5–9.

M1.justification: Section III retains the same SpikeSR architecture, spiking attention blocks, hybrid dimension attention, deformable similarity attention, and fusion block. The computational procedures and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AID for training, evaluate super-resolution on AID, DOTA, and DIOR, and use AID-tiny for ablations. The same 30-category AID breakdown and ×4 reconstruction examples remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding tables and qualitative comparisons. These retain methods such as CARN, LatticeNet, SwinIR-light, Omni-SR, SPIN, and HiT-SR, with no added or removed baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same 3,000 training and 900 validation AID images, bicubic degradation, Y-channel PSNR/SSIM evaluation, and model configurations. Training remains 1,000 epochs with batch size 4 and time step T = 4.

E4.justification: Tables III–V retain identical ablations of HDA/DSA, the feature pyramid, deformable convolution, and network depth. The feature visualizations and local attribution/diffusion-index analyses in Figures 8–9 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table I reports SpikeSR's average PSNR/SSIM as 31.95/0.8339 in both versions, and Tables III–IV retain the full model's 28.19 dB ablation result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Section III, including patch matching, deformable convolution, attention aggregation, and sequence fusion, are identical. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention-based spiking networks for efficient remote-sensing super-resolution, the proposed attention components, and competitive or state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of membrane-potential recalibration, self-similarity exploitation, patch misalignment, and performance–complexity tradeoffs are unchanged. No new applicability boundaries, failure conditions, or limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including Adam settings, learning rate, patch size, augmentation, channel configurations, and block counts. Both abstracts state that code will become available upon paper acceptance; no new access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section II retains the same discussion and positioning relative to deep super-resolution models, efficient models, and spiking networks. All 66 cited works remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The v2 byline adds Wenke Huang between Kui Jiang and Qiang Zhang, rewrapping the author names. The marginal arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose, terminology, headings, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables I–V retain the same graphics, captions, labels, formatting, and placement. The two-column page arrangement is unchanged; the author-list edit does not reorganize the document.

improvement.justification: The methods, evidence, mathematical content, interpretations, and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout both PDFs. The author-list and arXiv-stamp updates do not establish a meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's scientific or presentation quality.
